title: Ask (Grounded Question Answering) (Constrained, English)
cap_description: Answer a question over content with verbatim supporting quotes — fabricated evidence is a hard error
documentation:
## Purpose

`cat report.txt | ask --question "what caused the outage?"`: answers strictly from the content, with 1-5 VERBATIM quotes as evidence. The engine VERIFIES every quote actually occurs in the content (whitespace-normalized) — an answer resting on invented evidence is a hard error, never forwarded. When the content does not answer the question, the answer says so with empty quotes and confidence 0.0 — honest absence.

`searchx` finds WHERE; `ask` answers WHAT. Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The content to answer from (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--question`: the question (required).

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"answer": <string>, "quotes": [<verbatim excerpts>], "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<how the quotes support the answer>"}`.

## Notes

- Judgments are deterministic (law P4).

## Constrained
Marker indicating constrained generation: output is forced to satisfy a schema
or grammar. The model is guided so only valid tokens are sampled at each step;
output is structurally guaranteed.

The cap performs constrained generation.

## Language
The natural language of textual content. The `language` key carries an ISO-639
language code: `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, `fr` for French, and so on.
Caps that produce or consume language-specific content (summarisation, decision-
making, code generation) tag with the language they target.

English. ISO 639-1 code `en`.

args.name: question
args.arg_description: The question to answer about the content

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: Model spec to use for the judgment

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Semantic-judgment record: answer, verified verbatim quotes, confidence, reason

title: Classify (Closed-Set Labeling) (Constrained, English)
cap_description: Classify an item into exactly one of N allowed labels, with confidence and rationale
documentation:
## Purpose

The semantic router's workhorse: puts an item into exactly one of the labels you allow. `cat emails.ndjson | classify --labels urgent,billing,spam,personal` per item. The label is token-level constrained to the allowed set — a hallucinated label is impossible by construction.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The item to classify (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--labels`: 2-64 allowed labels, comma- or newline-separated, no duplicates (violations are hard errors naming the rule).
- An optional `--context` framing what the labels mean here.

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"label": <one of the allowed labels>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<one sentence>"}`.

## Notes

- Judgments are deterministic (law P4): same item, labels, and model produce the same label.

## Constrained
Marker indicating constrained generation: output is forced to satisfy a schema
or grammar. The model is guided so only valid tokens are sampled at each step;
output is structurally guaranteed.

The cap performs constrained generation.

## Language
The natural language of textual content. The `language` key carries an ISO-639
language code: `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, `fr` for French, and so on.
Caps that produce or consume language-specific content (summarisation, decision-
making, code generation) tag with the language they target.

English. ISO 639-1 code `en`.

args.name: labels
args.arg_description: Allowed labels: 2-64 names, comma- or newline-separated, no duplicates

args.name: context
args.arg_description: What the labels mean for this classification (one sentence)

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: Model spec to use for the judgment

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Semantic-judgment record: label (from the allowed set), confidence (0-1), reason (one sentence)

title: Coerce Boolean Array to String
cap_description: Convert an array of booleans to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a list of boolean values to a single string representation (e.g. `[true, false, true]`). Use this when a downstream cap expects a text value but the upstream produces a boolean array.

## Inputs

A list of boolean values (media type `media:bool;enc=utf-8;list`).

## Outputs

A string representation of the boolean array.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- For converting individual booleans, use [Coerce Boolean to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:bool;enc=utf-8";out="media:enc=utf-8").

title: Coerce Boolean to Integer
cap_description: Convert a boolean to an integer (true=1, false=0)
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a boolean value to an integer: `true` becomes `1`, `false` becomes `0`. Use this when a downstream cap expects an integer flag or count but the upstream produces a boolean.

## Inputs

A boolean value (media type `media:bool;enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

The integer `1` (true) or `0` (false).

## Notes

- Standard boolean-to-int mapping used across most programming contexts.
- To widen further to a float, chain with [Coerce Integer to Number](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:integer;numeric";out="media:numeric").

title: Coerce Boolean to Number
cap_description: Convert a boolean to a number (true=1.0, false=0.0)
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a boolean value to a floating-point number: `true` becomes `1.0`, `false` becomes `0.0`. Use this when a downstream cap expects a numeric type but the upstream produces a boolean.

## Inputs

A boolean value (media type `media:bool;enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

The float `1.0` (true) or `0.0` (false).

## Notes

- Use when connecting boolean outputs to numeric inputs (e.g. weight or scaling factors).
- For integer output instead, use [Coerce Boolean to Integer](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:bool;enc=utf-8";out="media:integer;numeric").

title: Coerce Boolean to Object
cap_description: Wrap a boolean value in a record
documentation:
## Purpose

Wraps a boolean value in a record (object) so it can be passed to caps that expect a structured record input. The boolean is stored under a standard key in the output record.

## Inputs

A boolean value (media type `media:bool;enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

A record containing the boolean value.

## Notes

- Use when a downstream cap requires a record type but the upstream produces a scalar boolean.
- This is primarily a type adapter for the capfab planner.

title: Coerce Boolean to String
cap_description: Convert a boolean value to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a boolean media value to its text string form (`"true"` or `"false"`). Use this when a downstream cap requires a string type but the upstream cap produces a boolean.

## Inputs

A boolean value (media type `media:bool;enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

The string `"true"` or `"false"`.

## Notes

- This is a type-level adapter for the capfab planner. The planner inserts coerce caps automatically when a boolean output needs to connect to a string input.
- For the reverse, see [Coerce String to Integer](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf-8";out="media:integer;numeric") or parse the string downstream.

title: Coerce Integer Array to String
cap_description: Convert an array of integers to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a list of integers to a single string representation. Use this when a downstream cap expects a text value but the upstream produces an integer array.

## Inputs

A list of integer values (media type `media:integer;list;numeric`).

## Outputs

A string representation of the integer array.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- For converting individual integers, use [Coerce Integer to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:integer;numeric";out="media:enc=utf-8").

title: Coerce Integer to Boolean
cap_description: Convert a integer value to a boolean
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a integer media value to a boolean (`true` / `false`). The missing inverse of the boolean→* coercion family: use it when a downstream cap requires a boolean but the upstream cap produces a integer.

## Inputs

A integer value (media type `media:integer;numeric`).

## Outputs

The boolean `true` or `false`.

## Notes

- Strict accepted spellings, nothing else: exactly `1` (true) and `0` (false). Anything outside that set is a hard error naming the accepted values — "truthiness" of arbitrary values would be a silent guess.
- This is a type-level adapter for the capfab planner, like the rest of the coerce family.

title: Coerce Integer to Number
cap_description: Widen an integer to a floating-point number
documentation:
## Purpose

Widens an integer to a floating-point number. Use this when a downstream cap requires a numeric (float) type but the upstream produces an integer.

## Inputs

An integer value (media type `media:integer;numeric`).

## Outputs

The same value as a floating-point number.

## Notes

- Widening conversion — no precision is lost for integers that fit in a 64-bit float (which is all practical integer values).
- For the narrowing direction (float to int), use [Coerce Number to Integer](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:numeric";out="media:integer;numeric") which truncates.

title: Coerce Integer to Object
cap_description: Wrap an integer value in a record
documentation:
## Purpose

Wraps an integer value in a record so it can be passed to caps that expect a structured record input.

## Inputs

An integer value (media type `media:integer;numeric`).

## Outputs

A record containing the integer value.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- Use when connecting an integer-producing cap to a record-consuming cap.

title: Coerce Integer to String
cap_description: Convert an integer value to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts an integer to its decimal string representation. Use this when a downstream cap requires a text value but the upstream produces an integer.

## Inputs

An integer value (media type `media:integer;numeric`).

## Outputs

The decimal string representation of the integer (e.g. `42` becomes `"42"`).

## Notes

- No locale-specific formatting — output is always plain decimal digits.
- For the reverse conversion, use [Coerce String to Integer](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf-8";out="media:integer;numeric").

title: Coerce Number Array to String
cap_description: Convert an array of numbers to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a list of floating-point numbers to a single string representation. Use this when a downstream cap expects text but the upstream produces a numeric array.

## Inputs

A list of numeric values (media type `media:list;numeric`).

## Outputs

A string representation of the number array.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- For converting individual numbers, use [Coerce Number to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:numeric";out="media:enc=utf-8").

title: Coerce Number to Boolean
cap_description: Convert a number value to a boolean
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a number media value to a boolean (`true` / `false`). The missing inverse of the boolean→* coercion family: use it when a downstream cap requires a boolean but the upstream cap produces a number.

## Inputs

A number value (media type `media:numeric`).

## Outputs

The boolean `true` or `false`.

## Notes

- Strict accepted spellings, nothing else: exactly `1`/`1.0` (true) and `0`/`0.0` (false). Anything outside that set is a hard error naming the accepted values — "truthiness" of arbitrary values would be a silent guess.
- This is a type-level adapter for the capfab planner, like the rest of the coerce family.

title: Coerce Number to Integer
cap_description: Truncate a numeric value to an integer
documentation:
## Purpose

Truncates a floating-point number to an integer by discarding the fractional part (toward zero). Use this when a downstream cap requires an integer but the upstream produces a float.

## Inputs

A numeric (float) value (media type `media:numeric`).

## Outputs

The integer part of the number (fractional part discarded, not rounded).

## Notes

- Truncation, not rounding: `3.9` becomes `3`, `-3.9` becomes `-3`.
- For the widening direction (no precision loss), use [Coerce Integer to Number](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:integer;numeric";out="media:numeric").

title: Coerce Number to Object
cap_description: Wrap a numeric value in a record
documentation:
## Purpose

Wraps a floating-point number in a record so it can be passed to caps that expect a structured record input.

## Inputs

A numeric (float) value (media type `media:numeric`).

## Outputs

A record containing the numeric value.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- Use when connecting a number-producing cap to a record-consuming cap.

title: Coerce Number to String
cap_description: Convert a numeric value to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a floating-point number to its string representation. Use this when a downstream cap requires a text value but the upstream produces a numeric value.

## Inputs

A numeric (float) value (media type `media:numeric`).

## Outputs

The string representation of the number.

## Notes

- Output format follows standard floating-point decimal notation.
- For the reverse conversion, use [Coerce String to Number](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf-8";out="media:numeric").

title: Coerce Object Array to String
cap_description: Convert an array of records to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a list of records to a single string representation. Use this when a downstream cap expects text but the upstream produces a list of objects.

## Inputs

A list of records (media type `media:list;record`).

## Outputs

A string representation of the record array.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- Output is typically serialized as a JSON array.
- For converting individual records, use [Coerce Object to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in=media:record;out="media:enc=utf-8").

title: Coerce Object to String
cap_description: Convert a record/object to its string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a record (object) to its string representation. Use this when a downstream cap requires text but the upstream produces a structured record.

## Inputs

A record value (media type `media:record`).

## Outputs

A string representation of the record.

## Notes

- The output format is typically JSON or a similar serialized form.
- For wrapping a string in a record (the reverse), use [Coerce String to Object](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf-8";out=media:record).
- For human-readable text output from a record, a format conversion cap (JSON-to-YAML, etc.) may produce better output than this coerce.

title: Coerce String Array to String
cap_description: Convert a list of strings to a single string representation
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a list of strings to a single string representation. Use this when a downstream cap expects a single text value but the upstream produces multiple strings.

## Inputs

A list of UTF-8 text strings (media type `media:enc=utf-8;list`).

## Outputs

A single string representing all items in the list (typically newline-separated or JSON array format).

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- If you need the items joined in a specific format (comma-separated, newline-separated, etc.), consider using a more explicit join operation upstream.

title: Coerce String to Boolean
cap_description: Convert a string value to a boolean
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a string media value to a boolean (`true` / `false`). The missing inverse of the boolean→* coercion family: use it when a downstream cap requires a boolean but the upstream cap produces a string.

## Inputs

A string value (media type `media:enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

The boolean `true` or `false`.

## Notes

- Strict accepted spellings, nothing else: `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off` (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed). Anything outside that set is a hard error naming the accepted values — "truthiness" of arbitrary values would be a silent guess.
- This is a type-level adapter for the capfab planner, like the rest of the coerce family.

title: Coerce String to Integer
cap_description: Parse a string value as an integer
documentation:
## Purpose

Parses a text string as an integer. Use this when a string-producing cap outputs a number as text (e.g. from a file or LLM output) and a downstream cap requires an integer type.

## Inputs

A UTF-8 text string value representing an integer (media type `media:enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

The parsed integer.

## Notes

- Fails hard if the input is not a valid integer string. Ensure upstream output is numeric text before using this coerce.
- For floating-point strings, use [Coerce String to Number](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf-8";out="media:numeric") instead.

title: Coerce String to Number
cap_description: Parse a string value as a number
documentation:
## Purpose

Parses a text string as a floating-point number. Use this when a string-producing cap outputs a numeric value as text and a downstream cap requires a numeric type.

## Inputs

A UTF-8 text string representing a number (media type `media:enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

The parsed floating-point number.

## Notes

- Fails hard if the string is not a valid numeric value.
- For integers specifically, use [Coerce String to Integer](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf-8";out="media:integer;numeric").
- For the reverse, use [Coerce Number to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:numeric";out="media:enc=utf-8").

cap_description: Wrap a string value in a record
documentation:
## Purpose

Wraps a string value in a record so it can be passed to caps that expect a structured record input. The string is stored under a standard key in the output record.

## Inputs

A UTF-8 text string value (media type `media:enc=utf-8`).

## Outputs

A record containing the string value.

## Notes

- Type adapter for the capfab planner.
- For the reverse, use [Coerce Object to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in=media:record;out="media:enc=utf-8").

title: Merge CSV Files
cap_description: Merge multiple CSV files into a single CSV file
documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of CSV files into a single CSV file. Headers from the first file are used; subsequent files contribute their data rows. Use this to fan-in results from parallel processing stages that each produce a CSV.

## Inputs

A sequence of CSV files (each with a header row and one or more data rows).

## Outputs

A single merged CSV file containing all rows from all inputs, with a single header.

## Notes

- All input CSVs must have compatible headers (same columns in the same order).
- Output preserves the row order of the inputs (first input rows appear first).
- For cross-format merging (CSV inputs to JSON or YAML output), use [Merge CSV Files into JSON Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record") or [Merge CSV Files into YAML List](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=yaml;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Single CSV file with all rows merged

title: Merge CSV Files into JSON Array
cap_description: Merge multiple CSV files into a single JSON array of objects
documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of CSV files into a single JSON array of objects, with each row becoming a JSON object and column headers becoming keys. Use this when downstream processing prefers JSON over CSV.

## Inputs

A sequence of CSV files (each with a header row and data rows).

## Outputs

A JSON array where each element is an object with keys from the CSV header and values from the row.

## Notes

- All input CSVs should have compatible headers.
- Useful for feeding CSV data into JSON-consuming caps or APIs.
- For keeping the output as CSV, use [Merge CSV Files](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=csv;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON array with all CSV rows as objects

title: Merge CSV Files into YAML List
cap_description: Merge multiple CSV files into a single YAML sequence of mappings
documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of CSV files into a single YAML sequence of mappings, with each row becoming a YAML mapping and column headers becoming keys. Use this when downstream processing prefers YAML.

## Inputs

A sequence of CSV files (each with a header row and data rows).

## Outputs

A YAML sequence where each element is a mapping with keys from the CSV header.

## Notes

- All input CSVs should have compatible headers.
- For JSON output, use [Merge CSV Files into JSON Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: YAML sequence with all CSV rows as mappings

title: Collect JSON Objects into Array
cap_description: Collect individual JSON objects into a single JSON array
documentation:
## Purpose

Gathers a sequence of individual JSON objects (one per pipeline item) into a single JSON array. Use this to fan-in results from parallel processing where each parallel branch produces one JSON object.

## Inputs

A sequence of JSON record objects.

## Outputs

A JSON array containing all input objects in order.

## Notes

- The objects do not need to have the same keys; heterogeneous objects are permitted.
- For CSV output, use [Collect JSON Objects into CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:fmt=json;record";out="media:fmt=csv;list;record").
- For YAML output, use [Collect JSON Objects into YAML List](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:fmt=json;record";out="media:fmt=yaml;list;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: JSON objects to collect into an array

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON array containing all input objects

title: Collect JSON Objects into CSV
cap_description: Collect individual JSON objects into a single CSV file
documentation:
## Purpose

Gathers a sequence of individual JSON objects into a single CSV file. Object keys become column headers; one row is written per object. Use this to produce tabular output from a fan-in of JSON-producing parallel stages.

## Inputs

A sequence of JSON record objects.

## Outputs

A CSV file with headers derived from the union of all object keys, and one row per object.

## Notes

- Objects with missing keys produce empty cells in those columns.
- Objects with different key sets are merged into a unified column set.
- For a JSON array output instead, use [Collect JSON Objects into Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:fmt=json;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: JSON objects to collect into a CSV

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: CSV file with one row per input object

title: Collect JSON Objects into YAML List
cap_description: Collect individual JSON objects into a single YAML sequence
documentation:
## Purpose

Gathers a sequence of individual JSON objects into a single YAML sequence of mappings. Each JSON object becomes one YAML mapping entry. Use this when downstream processing or configuration formats prefer YAML.

## Inputs

A sequence of JSON record objects.

## Outputs

A YAML sequence where each element is a mapping corresponding to one input JSON object.

## Notes

- Key order in the YAML output may differ from the JSON input; YAML mappings are unordered by spec.
- For a JSON array output, use [Collect JSON Objects into Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:fmt=json;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: JSON objects to collect into a YAML sequence

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: YAML sequence containing all input objects as mappings

title: Merge YAML Mappings into CSV
cap_description: Merge multiple YAML mapping files into a single CSV file
documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of YAML mapping files into a single CSV file. Each YAML mapping becomes one row; mapping keys become column headers. Use this to convert YAML-structured data from parallel processing stages into a tabular CSV for analysis or export.

## Inputs

A sequence of YAML mapping files (each file is a single YAML mapping, not a list).

## Outputs

A CSV file with headers from the union of all mapping keys and one row per input file.

## Notes

- Mappings with missing keys produce empty cells.
- For JSON array output, use [Merge YAML Mappings into JSON Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=yaml;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: CSV file with one row per YAML mapping

title: Merge YAML Mappings into JSON Array
cap_description: Merge multiple YAML mapping files into a single JSON array of objects
documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of YAML mapping files into a single JSON array of objects. Each YAML mapping becomes one JSON object. Use this to convert YAML-structured pipeline outputs into JSON for downstream caps that consume JSON arrays.

## Inputs

A sequence of YAML mapping files (each file is a single YAML mapping).

## Outputs

A JSON array where each element is an object derived from one input YAML mapping.

## Notes

- For YAML output, use [Merge YAML Mappings](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=yaml;record";out="media:fmt=yaml;list;record").
- For CSV output, use [Merge YAML Mappings into CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=yaml;record";out="media:fmt=csv;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON array containing all YAML mappings as objects

title: Merge YAML Mappings
cap_description: Merge multiple YAML mapping files into a single YAML sequence
documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of YAML mapping files into a single YAML sequence. Each mapping becomes one entry in the output list. Use this to fan-in YAML-producing parallel processing stages into a unified YAML document.

## Inputs

A sequence of YAML mapping files (each file is a single YAML mapping).

## Outputs

A single YAML sequence containing all input mappings as elements.

## Notes

- Preserves input order.
- For JSON array output, use [Merge YAML Mappings into JSON Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:fmt=yaml;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record").

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Single YAML sequence containing all input mappings

title: Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects
cap_description: Convert CSV data to a JSON array of objects with keys from the header row
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a CSV file into a JSON array of objects. Each data row becomes one JSON object; the CSV header row supplies the object keys. Use this when a downstream cap expects JSON but the data source is CSV.

## Inputs

A CSV file with a header row and one or more data rows.

## Outputs

A JSON array of objects, one per CSV row.

## Notes

- Column names from the header row become JSON keys. Sanitize column names upstream if they contain characters that are problematic as JSON keys.
- For YAML output, use [Convert CSV to YAML List of Mappings](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=yaml;list;record").
- For the reverse, use [Convert JSON Array of Objects to CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:fmt=json;list;record";out="media:fmt=csv;list;record").

title: Convert CSV to Text List
cap_description: Convert CSV data to a list of text values
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts CSV data into a flat list of text values. Use this when you need the raw cell values from a CSV as individual text items, discarding the row/column structure.

## Inputs

A CSV file.

## Outputs

A list of UTF-8 text values (cells flattened from the CSV).

## Notes

- Row and column structure is lost; the output is a flat sequence of cell values.
- If you need to preserve row structure, use [Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record") instead.

title: Convert CSV to YAML List of Mappings
cap_description: Convert CSV data to a YAML sequence of mappings with keys from the header row
documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a CSV file into a YAML sequence of mappings. Each data row becomes one YAML mapping; the CSV header row supplies the keys. Use this when a downstream cap or tool expects YAML but the data source is CSV.

## Inputs

A CSV file with a header row and one or more data rows.

## Outputs

A YAML sequence of mappings, one per CSV row.

## Notes

- For JSON output instead, use [Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:fmt=json;list;record").

title: Decimate Sequence
cap_description: Keep one item out of every N from an input sequence (drop the rest)
documentation:
## Purpose

Reduces the length of a sequence by keeping items at positions `0, N, 2N, ...` and dropping the rest. Useful for sub-sampling a long sequence — e.g. taking every 10th frame from `extract-frames`, every 5th record from a CSV, every Nth file from a folder.

## Inputs

- A sequence of any media type.
- An optional integer stride `N` (default: `1`, which is identity passthrough).

## Outputs

A sequence of the same media type as the input, containing approximately `ceil(input_count / N)` items. Per-item metadata on each kept item passes through unchanged.

## Notes

- The cap is generic over media (`in = media:`, `out = media:`); the planner routes it for any sequence input. The output's media URN matches the input's exactly — items themselves are passed through, not re-encoded.
- `--keep-every 1` (or omitting the argument) is exact passthrough.
- Negative, zero, or non-integer values fail loudly rather than silently being treated as 1; this is by design — a misspelled flag should surface, not be papered over.
- An empty input sequence is treated as a real input error (not a "successfully decimated zero items" success), since silently emitting an empty sequence would let downstream caps run on nothing without anyone noticing.

args.arg_description: Stride N: keep one item out of every N. Positive integer. Omit for passthrough.

outputs.output_description: Decimated sequence (same media type as input)

title: Edit (Instruction-Driven Transform)
cap_description: Transform JSON records by plain-language instruction via a generated, logged, deterministic program
documentation:
## Purpose

"Describe the transformation like you would to a chatbot, get a Unix tool": `edit --instruction "keep only active users, lowercase their emails, sort by name"` over a JSON array of records. The model translates the instruction into a program in a closed operation language (select/drop/rename/set/filter/map/sort/limit/reverse), token-level constrained to the program schema — an ill-formed program is impossible by construction. The program is logged in full BEFORE it runs, then executes deterministically. The model never touches the data: it sees only the instruction and a bounded structural sample (field names and types from the first records).

Fuzzy in, auditable and replayable out — the logged program re-run on tomorrow's file produces tomorrow's answer by the same rules.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md, Group 2).

## Inputs

- A JSON array of objects (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--instruction`: the transformation in plain language (required).

## Outputs

The transformed JSON array of records.

## Notes

- Program generation is deterministic (law P4): the same instruction and record structure produce the same program.
- Execution errors are hard and name the record index, field, and rule (e.g. lowercasing a number) — never silent skips.
- Requires the GGUF inference cartridge (constrained generation) to be installed.

CSV with uniform row width and normalized quoting.

title: Repair JSON
cap_description: Repair broken JSON with every fix logged — explicit forgiveness so strict caps can stay strict
documentation:
## Purpose

The explicit-forgiveness step of the semantic-primitive family (docs/semantic-primitives.md, law P9): the strict data caps stay strict, and when real-world input is broken — single quotes, unquoted keys, trailing or missing commas, Python literals (`True`/`None`), `NaN`/`Infinity`, comments, truncated documents — `repair` fixes it VISIBLY. Every fix is logged with its byte position and a one-sentence description, so a pipeline that needs leniency writes `repair | convert-…` and the leniency is on the record.

## Inputs

The broken JSON text (stdin or first positional argument).

## Outputs

Strictly valid JSON.

## Notes

- Valid JSON round-trips untouched (zero repairs logged) — repair is idempotent on clean input.
- Repairs happen only where the intended structure is unambiguous. Anything that would require guessing at DATA — trailing content after a complete document, unknown bare words — is a hard error naming the byte position. A wrong guess silently propagated is worse than a loud stop.
- Deterministic: no model is involved; the same input always repairs the same way.

args.arg_description: The broken JSON text to repair

title: Same (Semantic Equivalence) (Constrained, English)
cap_description: Judge whether two items refer to the same thing, with confidence and rationale
documentation:
## Purpose

The semantic `cmp`: decides whether two items refer to the same real-world thing — not whether they are textually equal. `same --context "company names in invoices" "OpenAI LLC" "Open AI"` returns `{"same": true, "confidence": 0.94, "reason": "spacing/legal suffix variation"}`. Use it in loops and joins wherever fuzzy identity matters: entity deduplication, record matching, reconciliation.

The first of the semantic-primitive cap family (see docs/semantic-primitives.md): Unix-style stdin→transform→stdout tools whose transform is a machine judgment with a guaranteed structured shape.

## Inputs

- The first item (stdin or first positional argument).
- The second item (second positional argument).
- An optional `--context` framing what "the same" means here (e.g. "company names on invoices"). One sentence; it configures the judgment, it is not a conversation.
- A model spec (defaults to the offline-travel-kit GGUF LLM).

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"same": <bool>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<one sentence>"}`. The shape is guaranteed by token-level constrained generation (LLGuidance) — downstream code parses it without error handling for malformed text.

## Notes

- Judgment caps are deterministic by default (temperature 0 semantics at the backend; law P4 in the design doc): the same items, context, and model produce the same judgment.
- Spelling variants, abbreviations, legal suffixes, and formatting differences do not make two references to one thing different; two genuinely different things are not the same however similar they look. The `reason` field names the decisive evidence.
- Served by the engine's generative-text cartridge over constrained GGUF inference (like [Make a Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:make-decision;constrained;in="media:enc=utf-8";language=en;out="media:decision;fmt=json;record")).

title: Save as Plain Text
cap_description: Persist a finalised plain-text value as a `.txt` file. Bytes pass through unchanged.
documentation:
## Purpose

Terminal cap for finalised plain text. The input must already carry the
`plain-text` marker — caps that produce user-facing prose (LLM text-generation,
OCR's digitized text, summarisation) declare `media:enc=utf-8;ext=txt;plain-text` as
their `out`, and this cap is the registered terminal that writes such values to
disk as `.txt`.

The narrow `in` is intentional. An earlier version accepted `media:enc=utf-8`,
which polluted the planner's recommended-paths surface — every text-producing
cap (PDF page extractor, JSON-as-text adapter, prompt loader) became a feeder
for `.txt` persistence even when the result wasn't meaningful prose. The
`plain-text` marker is an explicit "yes, this is finished text suitable for a
`.txt` file" opt-in.

## Inputs

- `media:enc=utf-8;ext=txt;plain-text` — finalised plain-text bytes.

## Outputs

The same bytes, same URN. The cap is a relabel-and-persist; the writer derives
the `.txt` extension from the URN's existing `file-type=txt` narrowing.

## Notes

- No conversion. No re-encoding. No content inspection. Byte-for-byte passthrough.
- To save text from a producer that emits `media:enc=utf-8` (not `plain-text`),
  the producer must be updated to declare the `plain-text` opt-in, OR a
  format-specific intermediate cap must be inserted to relabel the value.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The finalised plain-text value to persist as a `.txt` file

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: The same bytes, persisted as a `.txt` file

Turns a series of any frequency into one of a calendar period (daily to annual): each period with observations gets one value, combined by the aggregate chosen and stamped at the period's last observation.

- `every`: the period.

Periods with no observation are left out, not filled.

cap_description: Measure how a series changes: in percent, as a log ratio or as a difference, over so many observations
documentation:
## Purpose

Turns a series into its changes: each value compared with the one `over` observations before it.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `how`: percent, log or difference.
- `over`: how many observations back.

## Outputs

A time series of the changes, starting `over` observations in.

documentation:
## Purpose

Shifts a series so that each instant carries the value from `by` observations before, for comparing a series with its own past or leading one series against another.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `by`: how many observations.

The lagged series, starting `by` observations in.

Instants are kept; values move. The first `by` instants are left out.

documentation:

Turns a series into a rolling statistic: at each instant, the mean, standard deviation or z-score of the `window` observations ending there.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `window`: how many observations.
- `statistic`: mean, sd or zscore.

## Outputs

The rolling statistic, starting where the first full window ends.

A z-score over a window that does not move is left out for that instant and counted.

cap_description: Line several series up on the instants they all have
documentation:
## Purpose

Puts two or more series side by side on their shared instants.

## Inputs

- Two or more time series, gathered in the order the machine gives them.

## Outputs

Aligned series: each shared instant with every series' value, in input order.

## Notes

The series are interchangeable items of one list; a machine gathers them: `(a, b, c) -> align-series -> aligned`.

title: Combine Series
cap_description: Add, subtract, multiply or divide two series at the instants both have
documentation:
## Purpose

Combines a left and a right series value by value at their shared instants.

## Inputs

- `left`: a time series (the main input).
- `right`: a time series.
- `operation`: add, subtract, multiply or divide.

## Outputs

A time series of the results.

## Notes

Name the right-hand series in a machine: `(a, right=b) -> combine-series -> c`. Instants either lacks are left out; a division by zero leaves that instant out.

title: Filter Series
cap_description: Keep the observations of a series that pass a comparison with a threshold, and give those that fail on their own
documentation:
## Purpose

Splits a series by comparing each value with a threshold: the values that pass are the main output, those that do not an optional second output.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `keep`: above, below, at_least or at_most.
- `threshold`: the number compared with.

## Outputs

- `kept`: the observations that pass (always given, possibly empty).
- `dropped`: those that do not, given only when there are any, as the input's type.

## Notes

A router: `s -> filter-series -> (kept=k, dropped=d)`. What reads `dropped` is skipped when nothing was dropped.

Gives one summary of a series with the name of the summary taken.

A series summary: {summary, value}.

documentation:
## Purpose

Measures how much a dependent series moves with one or more regressors, on the instants they all have: `y = alpha + betas · x`.

## Inputs

- `y`: the dependent time series (the main input).
- `x`: one or more regressor series, in order.

## Outputs

- The regression (main output).
- `residuals`: what the fit leaves at each instant, as a time series.

## Notes

Runs a record program over a list of records, exactly as written, with no model involved.

Scores a record of forecasts of yes-or-no statements.

title: Try Forecasting Ways
cap_description: Try ways of forecasting a change in a series on its history: choose on each stretch, score on the next
documentation:
## Purpose

Hindcasts a statement about a series (will it end, or ever be, so many percent above or below where it stands, so many days ahead): through history, at moments `every-days` apart, each way of forecasting says a probability from what was known then; the moments are cut into stretches, the way that did best before each stretch is chosen and scored on it.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `comparison`, `change-pct`, `window`: the statement.
- `days`, `every-days`, `stretches`: the trial.

## Outputs

A forecast trial.

## Notes

A rule that only looked good on the history it was chosen on shows here as a chosen score no better than saying 50% every time.
